rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.

The clause 'the next module forks from the local commit' names what a LATER module (M5) will do -- the exact predicate-leak shape this rule calls out ('Any clause promising what a later beat will do is cartography however the sentence starts'), and it duplicates the maintainer block's own, more precise statement of the same fact (L81: "M5's worktree fork reads exactly that commit"). Deletion test: 'The commit is local, and that is the default. This is throwaway work you can reset away.' reads cleanly on its own. Countervailing read, why this is a TODO and not a confident finding: the clause also does double duty as the actual justification for why skipping the push (L40's optional prompt) is safe -- without it, a reader might wonder whether local-only leaves the commit unused. That tension is a genuine judgement call the maintainer is better placed to make than a rule-application.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either cut 'and the next module forks from the local commit' (let the sentence end at 'reset away', per the deletion test), or, if the M5-forks-from-local fact is doing load-bearing work justifying why pushing is optional, keep it but flag it as a deliberate keep-note in the maintainer block so a future judge doesn't re-flag it as cartography.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: commit-starting-point is one paragraph with three move-groups (create branch / append protected block / stage-commit-report) plus a sequential 'Then'; this is covered by the maintainer's explicit accept-note at L70 (sequential-build carve-out, moves cannot be reordered or read apart) and is NOT re-flagged here. Separately: take-task-end-to-end's second paragraph ('I'm leaving the laptop awake and walking away. Work through it. If you get stuck, write what you tried... If you finish, tell me what you shipped...') carries a framing move plus two conditional moves (stuck-case, finish-case) in one ~40-word paragraph, which is the named 'if X, do A; if Y, do B' move-boundary this rule calls out for a split. Read-aloud test is genuinely close, though: both conditionals are already separate, clearly-marked sentences, which mitigates the harm (Claude/student dropping a structural signal) the rule exists to prevent, and no maintainer accept-note covers this specific paragraph the way L68/L70 cover the other two edge cases in this file.
